title: A caregiver's comfort is how UNICEF says a baby's stress response settles
summary: UNICEF says a baby's stress response turns on when they are frightened or their needs are unmet, and that a caregiver's job is to help that response calm.
body: On a UNICEF Parenting class page about a baby's mental health, a stress response is described as turning on when babies become frightened or worry that someone has forgotten them or that their needs are not being met. The page says a parent's job is to help calm that response. When it calms, the page says, the baby learns that the world is a safe and reliable place. It also says that when children are under stress and do not have a loving adult to help them feel better, that can lay the groundwork for emotional difficulties later. The page is parenting teaching. It does not name a disorder, and it does not say a hard day predicts a later illness.
